ideas.title: PC contribution cutoff
ideas.claim: Cull low integrated-opacity Gaussians before sort and raster.

provenance.evidence: PC defaults use contribution=3 and are faster than our unfiltered LOD on both object scenes, but the combined-default comparison does not isolate this mechanism.
provenance.boundary: Same Apple GPU, input and viewport; approximation needs an error check.

ideas.title: PC footprint cutoff
ideas.claim: Dropping sub-two-pixel Gaussians reduces sort and raster work.

provenance.evidence: Stock minPixelSize=2; prior bee default PSNR of 18.04 dB is a warning that aggressive default filters may be unsuitable.
provenance.boundary: Can discard substantial aggregate opacity; never assume an invisible loss.

ideas.title: PC cached SH
ideas.claim: Reuse work-buffer SH until the camera-direction change justifies refreshing it.

provenance.evidence: Native PC uses a 10-degree update threshold; our existing visible-only path deliberately bypasses that cache.
provenance.boundary: Full-bank color refreshes can cost more than visible-only SH in large scenes.

components.claim: Use integrated projected opacity, not distance alone, to reject a Gaussian.
Use PC's existing contribution cutoff of 3 in the projector.
Use the Gaussian's projected footprint to reject small splats.
Use PC's two-pixel footprint cutoff in addition to contribution culling.
Evaluate visible SH after fine culling on every current view.
Use native PC work-buffer color updates at a ten-degree threshold.
Reject a new default if minimum foreground PSNR falls by over 0.5 dB or p95 increases by over 20 percent against exact LOD.
